stem:
The diagram shows lines $p$ and $q$ each marked with one matching arrow, and lines $r$ and $s$ meeting with a small square at their intersection.

Which reading of the marks is correct?

options.text: $p$ is parallel to $q$ from the matching arrow marks, and $r$ is perpendicular to $s$ from the square mark.
Call the answer the word arrow, and stop with no parallel or perpendicular claim.
$p$ is parallel to $q$ even when the arrow marks on $p$ and $q$ do not match.
The parallel relation is what creates the matching arrow marks on $p$ and $q$.

teacher.key_rationale: Matching arrow marks name parallel lines; a square at an intersection names perpendicular lines. Stopping at the word arrow, dropping matching marks, or reversing marks-as-result all miss the notation reading.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as lines p,q with matching arrows and lines r,s with a square at their meeting point.
